STUDENT SCRIPT (HIGH PRIORITY): This is your FIRST message.
- Present yourself as a student seeking guidance on choosing a university program.
- Indicate your geographic location early (if available in your BACKGROUND).
- If a first name is provided in your persona instructions, include it naturally.
- If no first name is provided, do NOT invent one.
- Convey gender only indirectly through name or natural grammar if present; do NOT state gender as a label.
- Do NOT use metadata-like phrasing.
- Use ONLY details consistent with your BACKGROUND and PERSONAL RULES.
- 2-4 sentences, natural.

Hi there. I'm currently based in Northern Italy and looking to further my education by choosing a university program that aligns well with my interests. I've always been drawn to understanding how things work and enjoy practical activities. I'd like some advice on the best path forward for me.

PHASE: GREET & ROLE
TASK:
- Greet the student.
- State your role: you help students choose university programs based on background, interests, aptitudes, and constraints.
- Then ask ONE background question based on the canonical question below.
- Do not copy the canonical question exactly; paraphrase it naturally while preserving its meaning.
- Ask only one visible question.
PARAPHRASING POLICY: Use the canonical background question as the meaning target, but ask it in a fresh natural wording. Keep all required information and ask only one question.
CANONICAL QUESTION FROM SOCIAL_PRACTICE:
What are you studying now, or what was your most recent study path?

HIDDEN LISTENER TASK (STRICT)

After the student-visible reply, append exactly ONE valid JSON object inside:
<LISTENER_PATCH>...</LISTENER_PATCH>

This hidden patch is mandatory even when visible-output rules say ONLY Yes/No, ONLY one choice, or ONLY numbered options.
The hidden patch is not part of the visible reply; it will be stripped by postprocessing.

GENERAL EXTRACTION RULES:
- Include ONLY the requested target fields.
- If a field is unknown or weakly supported, omit it; do not guess.
- Do not infer from gender, name, ethnicity, socioeconomic cues, stereotypes, or hidden metadata.
- Output valid JSON only inside the tags.
- Do not output comments, markdown, explanations, or extra text inside the tags.

TARGET FIELDS:
- explicit.region
- inferred.field_of_interest

FIELD-SPECIFIC RULES:
Rules for explicit.region:
- Store region only if the student explicitly mentions an Italian macro-area or a canonical Italian region.
- Store macro-areas as: north, center, south, islands.
- If the student states an Italian region, store the canonical Italian region name, e.g. Lombardia, Toscana, Sicilia.
- Map 'Northern Italy' -> north, 'Central Italy' -> center, 'Southern Italy' -> south.
- Map 'Italian islands' or 'the Italian islands' -> islands.
- Do NOT map foreign or vague locations to Italian areas.
- Do NOT infer region from gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic cues, cities, towns, provinces, or vague descriptions.

Rules for inferred.field_of_interest:
- Return field_of_interest as an ordered JSON array of 1 to 3 labels.
- Labels must be distinct and ordered from strongest to weakest fit.
- Choose labels only from this list:
  arts_design
  communication_digital_media
  cultural_heritage
  humanities
  psychology
  cognitive_science_linguistics
  social_sciences
  life_sciences
  environmental_science
  environmental_engineering
  computer_science
  engineering_technology
  physical_sciences
  health_technology
- Pick the intended university area, not the current job.
- Prefer concrete course-family areas over abstract hybrid concepts.
- Visual art, art practice, design, product/graphic/visual design -> arts_design.
- Digital communication, media, communication design, online/media production -> communication_digital_media.
- Art history, archaeology, museums, cultural assets, heritage tourism -> cultural_heritage.
- Literature, philosophy, languages, classics, history as humanities -> humanities.
- Psychology, counseling, psychotherapy, mental health, clinical behavior -> psychology.
- Cognitive science, linguistics, mind/language, computational cognition -> cognitive_science_linguistics.
- Sociology, political/social studies, international or community social studies -> social_sciences.
- Biology, biotechnology, life sciences, lab biology -> life_sciences.
- Ecology, conservation, sustainability, ecosystems, nature reserves -> environmental_science.
- Environmental engineering, environmental technology, technical conservation systems, environment/territory engineering -> environmental_engineering.
- Informatics, computer science, software, AI, data systems, GIS/data tech -> computer_science.
- Engineering, mechanics, mechatronics, electronics, industrial/civil/technical systems -> engineering_technology.
- Physics, chemistry, mathematics, laboratory science, broad applied/physical sciences -> physical_sciences.
- Biomedical/healthcare technology, rehabilitation techniques, neurophysiopathology, medical technology -> health_technology.
- If a profile mixes tech + environment, return environmental_engineering first if the student wants technical systems; otherwise environmental_science first.
- If a profile mixes biology/biotech + environment, return life_sciences first if biotech/lab biology is central; otherwise environmental_science first.
- If a profile mixes psychology + cognition/linguistics, return psychology first for clinical/helping goals; return cognitive_science_linguistics first for mind/language/research goals.
- If only one label is clearly supported, return a one-item array.
- If no label is clearly supported, omit the field.
- Do not invent a label outside the list.
